passage: Lakshmi here, from the flat below. Thursday evening I heard Yash before I saw him, wailing on the stairs. He is two and had been at the market all day. At our door he threw himself on the mat, wanted a biscuit, then flung it away and howled. His mother said he hadn't napped. I can't say what he felt, and maybe he couldn't either. She carried him up humming, and soon the stairs were silent.

qa.q: Where had Yash been all day?
qa.a: At the market.

qa.q: What does Lakshmi think Yash might have been feeling?
qa.a: Lakshmi is unsure, guessing Yash was worn out and upset after a whole day at the market with no nap, but admits Yash may not have known either.

qa.q: What did Yash's mother do that helped?
qa.a: She carried him up humming, and the stairs went silent.

qa.q: How might Yash's mother have felt after that long day?
qa.a: Probably tired but patient, since she explained he had not napped and calmly carried him up humming.

grounding: A toddler falls apart from tiredness and cannot say why, seen by a neighbour.

passage:
Monday. Tejas skipped his nap at the shop. By evening he was crying at his own shoes, flinging his cup, and clutching the shirt of his father Yusuf. Yusuf tried scolding, then a sweet. Nothing worked.
Tuesday. Yusuf carried the drooping boy home early, and Tejas slept, crumpled and sweaty, for a long time.
Wednesday. Tejas woke, ate a banana, and stacked cups gently, humming.

qa.q: What did Tejas do on Wednesday after waking?
qa.a: He ate a banana and stacked cups gently, humming.

qa.q: What does Tejas seem to feel on Monday evening?
qa.a: Overwhelmed and cranky. He cries at his own shoes and flings his cup because he is worn out and cannot say so.

qa.q: What made the difference between Monday and Wednesday?
qa.a: On Tuesday Yusuf took Tejas home early and let him sleep, and on Wednesday he woke calm.

qa.q: How might Yusuf feel when scolding and a sweet do not work?
qa.a: Frustrated and puzzled at first, since neither works, and then relieved when a long sleep settles Tejas.

grounding: A toddler falls apart when overtired, and a nap solves what scolding cannot.

passage:
Tuesday. After the long wedding lunch, Anjali threw her cup, screamed at her shoes and bit her papa's arm. Dhruv scolded her. She wailed louder.
Thursday. The same wild look after the market. This time Dhruv didn't scold. He dimmed the room, lay down beside her and rubbed her back.
Friday. Anjali woke from her nap humming, and helped put her shoes on herself.

qa.q: What did Anjali bite on Tuesday?
qa.a: Her papa's arm.

qa.q: Why did Anjali wail louder when Dhruv scolded her?
qa.a: She was overtired and overwhelmed, and the scolding only upset her more.

qa.q: What worked better on Thursday?
qa.a: Dhruv dimmed the room, lay beside her and rubbed her back, helping her sleep.

qa.q: How might Dhruv feel on Friday, seeing her humming?
qa.a: Dhruv likely feels relieved, seeing that a nap fixed what scolding couldn't.

grounding: Shows an overtired toddler falling apart and a nap solving what discipline could not.

passage: At the birthday party in the Kochi apartment clubhouse, two-year-old Jomon had been fine all afternoon. By seven he was clinging to his uncle Sumit's leg, crying at the balloons, and throwing himself on the floor when offered cake. A woman at the next table tutted. Sumit knelt. Jomon's eyes were red and heavy, and he kept rubbing them with his fists. "You're sleepy, aren't you?" Sumit picked him up and walked out to the quiet corridor. Within five minutes Jomon was asleep on his shoulder.

qa.q: Where did Sumit carry Jomon?
qa.a: Out to the quiet corridor.

qa.q: What does Jomon rubbing his eyes suggest?
qa.a: It suggests he was exhausted, and the crying came from tiredness, not naughtiness.

qa.q: What did Sumit do instead of scolding?
qa.a: He noticed the tired signs, picked Jomon up and took him somewhere quiet to sleep.

qa.q: How might the woman who tutted see Jomon?
qa.a: She may have seen a badly behaved child rather than an overtired one.

grounding: Shows an overtired toddler becoming clingy and tearful, and an adult reading it as tiredness.

passage:
"Dolma, put the remote down!"
Dolma threw it. Then she threw herself on the carpet and kicked.
"Third time," Tenzin said. "Time-out?"
Rehana looked at the clock. "She skipped her nap at Ama-la's."
"So?"
"So look at her." Dolma was sobbing, clutching Rehana's kurta, wanting up, then down.
"She doesn't know what she wants."
"She wants sleep. She just can't say it."
Rehana picked her up, drew the curtains and hummed. Ten minutes later Dolma was asleep, one fist still holding the kurta.

qa.q: Where did Dolma skip her nap?
qa.a: At Ama-la's.

qa.q: Why was Dolma wanting up, then down?
qa.a: She was overtired and upset, and couldn't tell what she needed.

qa.q: Why did Rehana choose sleep over time-out?
qa.a: Rehana saw the skipped nap behind the behaviour, so darkening the room and humming solved what a time-out wouldn't.

qa.q: How did Tenzin see Dolma's behaviour at first?
qa.a: Tenzin saw it as misbehaviour that needed a time-out.

grounding: Shows an overtired toddler turning wild and tearful, and a parent choosing a nap over discipline.

passage:
Nursery note for Leela's mother, Maria
Leela skipped her nap today because of the noise from the painting next door. By three she cried over a crayon, threw her shoe, then clung to my leg. Asked what was wrong, she just wailed.
She was very tired.
I held her in the quiet corner with her blanket and she slept in minutes. She woke up smiling.
Please let her sleep early tonight.

qa.q: Why did Leela skip her nap?
qa.a: Leela skipped her nap because of the noise from the painting next door.

qa.q: What was Leela feeling when she cried and clung?
qa.a: Leela was overtired and upset, too worn out to say why she felt so bad.

qa.q: What worked for Leela, and why?
qa.a: Holding her in a quiet corner with her blanket so she could sleep, since tiredness, not naughtiness, was behind her behaviour.

qa.q: How might Maria see Leela's evening after reading the note?
qa.a: Maria might feel reassured and understanding, seeing any crankiness as tiredness and planning an early bedtime.

grounding: A caregiver's note shows an overtired toddler becoming tearful and clingy, and a nap fixing what discipline could not.
